cross_cutting_mbo_finding: THE EIA THURSDAY IS HALF BUILT BEFORE THE PRINT, AND THE FIRST SIXTY SECONDS AFTER IT DECIDE WHETHER THAT HALF SURVIVES. Across all fourteen EIA Thursdays in g17-g23, the pre-print window's share of the day's absolute travel has median 49.5% (IQR ~34-59%) - the window is not a coil, it is half the session, and on my day it held the session high fifty-four seconds before the release. What the print supplies is not a direction but an ARBITER function, and it is measurable in the tape's first minute. On the six Thursdays that entered 10:30 with a chain-sided UP run of at least +300, the sixty-second impulse separates the outcomes without a single exception across five groups: an impulse inside +/-300 and the run continues (0416 +720, 0430 +1230, 0528 +2100, 0604 +1130), an impulse at or beyond -300 and the run round-trips in full and closes negative (0625 -60, 0716 -20). The separation is clean at 30, 60 and 120 seconds and starts to fail at 300, which places the arbiter inside the first two minutes - exactly where the standing NYMEX-canary lag says the information is. Underneath that sits the block's real structural fact, which is not Thursday-specific at all: on this tape heavy BUY aggression does not deliver price and heavy SELL aggression is unremarkable. Same-day signed flow versus same-day price across all seventy sessions - buy >+1000 agrees 41%, >+1500 29%, >+2000 25%, >+3000 20%, monotone; sell over the identical thresholds flat at 46/43/46/47%. At >+3000, eight of the ten days closed down and six carry absorb_session=true. The same quantity measured one day EARLIER is a coin flip (4/9), which is how my blind came to treat 0715's +6,326 - the largest buy flow in seven groups - as its bullish evidence for a day that closed -20. It was reading a same-day bearish tell as a next-day bullish one.

days.magnitude_derivation: NOT fitted - three independent derivations that converge, none of which uses the realized close. (1) PRE-DECLARED CLASS: my own blind named the branch and its bound - 'a COUNTER (loose) print in S1-void ROUND-TRIPS to the flat class per magnitude.shoulder_counter_print_damping (mirrored ~0..-300)'. The print delivered counter, so that is the branch that fires and its band is 0..-300. My error was never the scenario library; it was the 0.27 weight I put on the branch that was right. (2) THE ROUND-TRIP PATH, from the only comparable instance available (0625, g22, the other decisive-counter-impulse day on a pre-print UP run): the day overshoots to about -1.4x the pre-print run and then reclaims about 54% of that excursion, closing near -0.10x the run. Pre-print run here R=+560 -> overshoot ~-780 (realized -770) -> close ~-56. On 0625 the same arithmetic gives R=+340 -> -490 (realized -490) -> close -34 (realized -60). (3) THE PHASE TABLE: phase 3 carries +3,966 of signed BUY flow against +460 of price - conviction ALIGNED, and the largest single-phase buy flow in the block (next largest 0715 phase 3 at +3,342). A closing phase with the block's largest aligned buy does not settle at the bottom of its class, so the close belongs at the TOP of the 0..-300 band: 0 to -100. Derivations (2) and (3) both land -50..-60; I emit -60 and I do NOT claim the last 40 points to the actual -20.

target_1_what_owned_the_blocks_down_move.what_this_does_to_my_blame: It exonerates my SIGN and convicts my SCALE. The roll-free regime of this block ran at roughly +105 per day and my day was the flattest of the four. A +300 net call is about three times the roll-free regime's own daily scale and about fifteen times my day's realized magnitude. The whole 320 of blind error is magnitude; the direction miss is two ticks on a day that closed 2.898 against a 2.900 prior close, and calling that a direction error at all is an artifact of scoring sign on a flat day.
target_1_what_owned_the_blocks_down_move.the_thing_my_blind_got_backwards: My blind read 'in_gsci_roll FALSE at BD11, the window closed 0714, no roll-flow overlay' as SUPPORT for the up-chain - the mechanical seller has left, so the buyers win. The measured record says the opposite: with the roll's selling gone, the tape stopped moving. The roll was not suppressing an up move; the roll WAS the move. Remove it and the daily scale collapses toward zero. A roll window ending is a MAGNITUDE event, not a direction event, and I traded it as a direction event.

target_2_my_print_decomposed_the_0709_wa.the_mirror_test_verdict: MY PRINT IS NOT 0709'S MIRROR - IT IS 0709'S OPPOSITE MECHANISM, and that is the finding. On 0709 the print itself was inert (about 5% of the move, -100 reclaimed in 40 seconds) and the damage was a LIQUIDITY-VOID reprice: -1,860 delivered on signed flow of -11 across 98,400 lots, into a mid book with no short base to arrest it; absorb_session TRUE. On 0716 the print's own minute carried 18% of the travel - three and a half times 0709's share - and the delivery that followed was genuine ALIGNED aggression, not a void: phase 2 signed flow -2,776 against -430 of price, conviction +1, absorb_session FALSE. Real sellers hit real bids. Same lens, same block, consecutive prints, opposite microstructure. Pooling these two into an 'EIA Thursday' average would destroy both readings.
target_2_my_print_decomposed_the_0709_wa.why_the_magnitudes_differ_by_a_hundred_f: Because of what met the delivery. 0709 had no short base and fell 2,050. 0716 had one: phase 3 delivered +3,966 of aggressive buying, the block's largest single-phase buy, and reclaimed 750 of the 850 delivery. The base that damped my day is the same accumulation my blind cited as its bullish evidence (0714 +3,747, 0715 +6,326). Those flows were real and they mattered - but they were MAGNITUDE DAMPING, available to arrest a fall, not DIRECTION. I read a shock absorber as an engine.
target_2_my_print_decomposed_the_0709_wa.how_much_was_the_print_surprise_itself: The print was +41 Bcf for week ending 0710 (revealed in the 0717 state row: level 3024, weekly_chg 41, vs_5yr 162). Against the ~45 Bcf figure our own consensus_poll collector carried and the investing.com route cross-validated, +41 is a BULLISH surprise - tighter than the survey, and far under the prior week's +61. My blind's PHYSICAL forecast was correct: it predicted 'a SMALL injection, visibly under the ~+45-55 5yr-average class and far under the prior +61' from the ngwu balance tightening, and the print delivered exactly that. THE MARKET SOLD A BULLISH SURPRISE BY 1,410 POINTS IN THIRTY-THREE MINUTES. So the answer to 'how much was the print's own surprise' is: the surprise SIGN contributed nothing, because it was pointed the other way. What the print contributed was the ARBITER function - a scheduled moment at which the pre-print run had to be defended and was not.
target_2_my_print_decomposed_the_0709_wa.what_this_confirms_in_my_own_lens_file: My lens file already says it in one line - 'Surprise SIGN does not reliably sort direction; delivery-vs-absorption in the first post-print phases does.' My blind read that line and then built its entire up-lean on a physically-implied tight print. The failure was not a missing rule; it was a live rule I overrode with a fundamental story. Cross-group check on the same quantity (the print's own surprise measured against the 5-year norm, i.e. the vs_5yr WoW delta revealed at 10:30, n=7 over g20-g23): sorts the day 3/7 clean with 2 flats. It does not sort. The lens line stands and is now measured, not asserted.

target_3_burn_gate_adjudication.adjudication: I CONCUR WITH THE REFUTATION AS WRITTEN, and I add the term the other three refutations did not reach. D-0709 showed the CDD-add limb is a CONSTANT (positive 20/20 at h1 on the S110-grafted ladder) and therefore cannot gate, and that grid_stack is D+2 stale so the burn confirmation is structurally backward-looking. Both hold on my day and I do not restate them. E's mechanism - when the balance loosens at the demand peak, burn confirmation is BEARISH information - is the correct diagnosis, and my day is the cleanest instance of it available anywhere in the seven groups.
target_3_burn_gate_adjudication.why_my_day_is_the_clean_instance: Every term was at its bullish extreme and the market still refused. Burn at a block high. CDD at its seasonal crest (D0 16.8, the highest forecast CDD of the block). And the print itself came in BULLISH versus the survey (+41 against ~45). Peak burn, peak heat, a tighter-than-expected print - and NG fell 1,410 points in thirty-three minutes. There is no weather or conversion story left standing after that. The only thing that explains it is the denominator.
target_3_burn_gate_adjudication.the_denominator_is_measurable_and_it_is_: It is storage.vs_5yr and its week-over-week delta, which is already in the served state on every single day and needs no new feed. The visible trajectory at my decision time: vs_5yr 112 (as_of 06-18) -> 151 (07-02) -> 156 (07-09). The surplus WIDENED five Bcf into the demand crest with burn at a block high. Then my print widened it again to 162 - on a +41 injection, because the 5-year norm for that week was about +35. Read together with the weekly change collapsing 87 -> 61 -> 41, the two series say the thing the gate cannot: the NUMERATOR was tightening every week and the BALANCE was loosening every week anyway. Burn is a numerator with no balance-clearing denominator, exactly as E put it, and vs_5yr is the denominator sitting unused in the same JSON blob.
target_3_burn_gate_adjudication.would_es_successor_have_sorted_my_day: YES on my day, and I will not overstate it beyond that. Both terms were decision-time-visible: vs_5yr 156 and its +5 WoW widening are in the 0716 state row, and the prior 151 is in the 0709 row of the same served file, so the delta is computable by a blind agent with no extra data. Tested honestly as a GATE REVOCATION - does a widening surplus revoke a burn-licensed up-call - it is right on 0709 (+39 widening, day -2,050) and right on 0716 (+5 widening, day -20) and WRONG on 0618 (+33 widening, day +520). Two of three, n=3 across two groups. Tested as a standalone day-direction sorter it is 4/7 and I make no such claim for it. It belongs in the gate as the missing denominator, not in the brain as a direction rule.
target_3_burn_gate_adjudication.what_separates_0618_from_0709_and_0716: The candidate is the CDD ladder's slope: 0625 +1.1 (heat still building), 0702 -5.9, 0709 -2.1, 0716 -4.0 (all three crested). A widening surplus while more heat is still coming is attributable to a weather lag; a widening surplus with the ladder rolling over is structural. But the ladder does not exist in the g21 state at all, so 0618 cannot be tested on it, and the two days that DO satisfy the crest-plus-widening conjunction (0709, 0716) are both in g23. n=2 in ONE group. I name it and I do NOT propose it - it does not span groups and I will not dress up a same-group pair as a general rule.
target_3_burn_gate_adjudication.attribution_fence_observed: The S110 ladder graft changed weather_forecast under both g22 and g23, so I bank neither credit nor blame on any CDD-ladder quantity, including the crest read immediately above, which is one of the two reasons it stays below the bar. The storage block carries no graft: vs_5yr, weekly_chg and level come from the unmodified store on every group, so the denominator claim is made on an input that did not move underneath it.

days.confidence_note: Magnitude 0.74 - three independent derivations converge inside 10 dollars of each other and the class was pre-declared by the blind itself, so I am not inventing a number. Direction is deliberately NOT the object of confidence on this day: a -20 close is inside any honest band's noise and I decline to claim a direction hit. Timing 0.85 - the onset (08:05), the arbiter (10:30:01), the delivery low (11:08) and the covering leg (14:00-15:00) are all stamped in the evidence file or plainly resolved in the downsampled tape. days.weight_note: The blind keeps a real share, and the reason is specific rather than generous. It owned the pre-print window's DIRECTION correctly (up, on coherent D-1 flow, per the doctrine's rule that direction stays with the D-1 tilt) and that window turned out to hold the day's entire up move and its session high. It also pre-declared the exact branch and the exact bound that the day landed in. Both of those are core-model work and the posterior is built on top of them, not instead of them. But the blind put the catalyst mass on the wrong side of 10:30 and weighted its correct branch at 0.27, and neither error is recoverable from the blind's own information set - the print-impulse arbiter is a causal observation and nothing else resolves it. Hence the majority to the causal layer, and hence a posterior that CORRECTS the blind's time-placement rather than reversing its read of the chain.

proposal_contribution.note: TEXT ONLY - no brain edit is made or implied. Each item carries its own n, the groups it spans, its scope and its falsifier. Items that do not clear the n>=2-spanning-groups bar are listed separately and are NOT proposed.

clears_the_bar.statement: On an EIA Thursday that arrives at 10:29 carrying a chain-sided UP run of at least +300 from the prior close, the sixty seconds after 10:30 adjudicate the run. An impulse inside +/-300 confirms it and the day continues up; an impulse at or beyond -300 rejects it and the day round-trips the run in full and closes at or below flat. Do not carry a chain-sided sign THROUGH the print - carry it TO the print and let the first minute decide.
clears_the_bar.mechanism: The pre-print run is inventory, not conviction: it is built by desks positioning for the number. The print is the scheduled moment at which that inventory must be defended. A counter impulse means the inventory is being liquidated by the people who built it, which is why the round-trip overshoots rather than stopping at flat.
clears_the_bar.scope: Pre-print UP runs only. On the five Thursdays entering 10:29 with a run of -300 or worse, no sixty-second impulse reached |300| at all, so the rule has nothing to say there and must not be applied symmetrically.
clears_the_bar.falsifier: A pre-print-UP Thursday whose sixty-second impulse is at or beyond -300 and which still closes materially up, or one whose impulse stays inside +/-150 and which nonetheless round-trips.
clears_the_bar.forward_test: G24+ EIA Thursdays. Two fires and four declines is thin, and the deflationary reading - that this is ordinary first-minute momentum - is not excluded by n=6. What would distinguish it is the 0604 case, where a mild counter (-110) failed to stop a +1130 day; a momentum rule would have faded that.
clears_the_bar.directly_repairs: daytype.eia_preprint_overextension_gate, whose stated purpose is my chain-through-the-print flaw. The gate is a PRE-print check and on my day it correctly declined to fire (D-1 flow was genuinely coherent, 0.546 against 0.560). The flaw it targets is not fully addressable before 10:30; this supplies the post-10:30 half.

clears_the_bar.statement: When the arbiter above fires counter on a pre-print UP run of size R, the existing play's flat 0..-300 band should be replaced by a PATH: the day overshoots to roughly -1.4R below the prior close, then reclaims about 54% of that excursion, closing near -0.10R.
clears_the_bar.mechanism: The liquidation runs past flat because the inventory being sold was accumulated above the prior close; it stops where the accumulation started. The reclaim is the other side of that same inventory being re-bought once the forced flow is done - which is why it is roughly half and not all.
clears_the_bar.evidence: n=2 spanning 2 groups. 0625 g22: R=+340, overshoot -490 (1.44R), reclaim 51.8%, close -60; the formula predicts -34. 0716 g23: R=+560, overshoot -770 (1.34R), reclaim 55.7%, close -20; the formula predicts -56. Both within 40 of the realized close.
clears_the_bar.scope: Only on a fired counter-print arbiter following a pre-print UP run. Not a general reversal-sizing rule.
clears_the_bar.falsifier: A third counter-print fire whose overshoot is under 1.0R, or whose reclaim falls outside roughly 25-85%.
clears_the_bar.forward_test: The next counter-print fire in G24+. n=2 is the minimum bar and the coefficients (1.4, 54%, -0.10) should be treated as the shape of the claim, not as calibrated constants; the robust part is 'overshoots the round trip, reclaims about half, closes near flat'.

clears_the_bar.statement: On this NG tape, large SAME-DAY net BUY aggression is a bearish-to-null tell and the effect strengthens monotonically with size; large net SELL aggression carries no comparable information. The same quantity measured on D-1 carries no information in either direction, so this is a live nowcast, not a next-day direction input - and it must never be used as one.
clears_the_bar.mechanism: Persistent offer-side supply above the market (producer hedging, index roll selling, call overwriting) feeds aggressive buyers, so lifting the offer in size marks distribution. There is no symmetric bid-side wall, so hitting bids in size marks nothing. This is the standing dipole divergence read in its NG-specific, one-sided form.
clears_the_bar.scope: Same-day, session-level signed flow on the NG leg. Not tested on WTI and not to be assumed there.
clears_the_bar.falsifier: A run of >+3000 buy-flow sessions closing up, or the monotone gradient across thresholds flattening on G24+.
clears_the_bar.forward_test: G24+, and it should be watched specifically for era-dependence - a structural offer-side supply story can change when the hedging or index-roll regime changes.

summary: 0716 was decided in the sixty seconds after 10:30 and it went the other way from my blind's +300, but the interesting part is that the blind was right about the leg it owned and wrong about where the day's mass sat. The reopen-to-10:29 window delivered +560 and set the session HIGH at 10:29:06 - fifty-four seconds before the print - confirming my own reopen->print play's window assignment while refuting its +110 mass claim by five times. The print then rejected the run: -570 in nine seconds, a 350-point reclaim, then a delivery to -770 by 11:08, then a covering rally that took back 56% of the overshoot for a -20 close. Unlike 0709, nothing here was a liquidity void - all three phases were flow-ALIGNED (-101/-60, -2,776/-430, +3,966/+460) and absorb_session is FALSE, so the near-zero net is the cancellation of two convicted legs, not a quiet day. The print itself came in at +41 Bcf against a ~45 survey - a BULLISH surprise - and the market sold it 1,410 points, because the balance was loosening regardless: the surplus ran 151 to 156 to 162 while injections collapsed 87 to 61 to 41. My blind forecast that tight print correctly from the ngwu balance and was paid nothing for it. Posterior -60 (actual -20), derived three independent ways, none fitted.
